Alexandrium.risk_note: Harmful algal bloom (PSP and other syndromes) linked to nutrient enrichment in coastal systems

Asterionellopsis glacialis.risk_note: Coastal diatom frequent in productive, well‑flushed waters

Cerataulina.risk_note: Marine diatom associated with nutrient‑rich upwelling or mixed coastal waters

Ceratium.risk_note: Blooms in stratified coastal waters influenced by nutrient inputs

Chaetoceros.risk_note: Dominant genus in high‑nutrient coastal and upwelling systems; spores record eutrophication events

Entomoneis.risk_note: Benthic/periphytic genus typical of moderately enriched but not heavily polluted habitats

Guinardia.risk_note: Common in productive coastal waters with elevated chlorophyll a

Hemiaulus.risk_note: Oceanic diatom, often with N2‑fixing symbionts, typical of relatively low‑nutrient waters

Lauderia annulata.risk_note: Coastal diatom of well‑mixed, nutrient‑rich but not extremely polluted waters

Nitzschia.risk_note: Many species tolerant to organic pollution, variable salinity and eutrophication; widely used as pollution indicators

Noctiluca.risk_note: Visible red/green tides associated with organic enrichment and dense phytoplankton in coastal systems

Ornithocercus magnificus.risk_note: Warm‑water oceanic taxon typical of relatively unpolluted offshore waters

Pinnularia.risk_note: Freshwater benthic genus with many species used as indicators of good ecological status

Pleurosigma.risk_note: Benthic diatom of productive coastal sediments, often linked to moderate organic enrichment

Prorocentrum.risk_note: Several toxic HAB species (e.g. P. minimum) linked to anthropogenic nutrient enrichment

Protoperidinium.risk_note: Heterotrophic dinoflagellate that increases with high phytoplankton biomass in enriched systems

Pyrodinium.risk_note: Highly toxic HAB genus in tropical coastal waters subject to strong nutrient inputs

Thalassionema.risk_note: Marine diatom common in productive coastal waters with good oxygenation

Thalassiosira.risk_note: Key coastal and upwelling genus dominating in high‑nutrient waters; used as indicator of eutrophication

_meta.note: Trophic categories are qualitative (oligotrophic, mesotrophic, eutrophic) and pollution_tolerance (0–1) is a heuristic index derived from published information on diatom and dinoflagellate indicator values, eutrophication responses and HAB occurrence, not from a single standardized index.
